goal: A store's own domain is resolved when the request arrives: the proxy looks the host up (one indexed read, remembered for 60 seconds per instance), serves the store's pages and files from /s/{store}, and sends the store's other addresses to its primary; next.config.ts compiles no rule per store domain, and activating, removing or re-pointing a domain asks for no deployment.
why: Today every store domain is compiled into each deployment: 4 to 8 routing rules per domain against Vercel's cap of 2,048 (the app's own routes take about 705), a ceiling near 270 stores with a domain, and a full production deploy per domain change. After: .next/routes-manifest.json holds the same number of redirects and rewrites with 0 or 300 active store domains, and a domain activated after the build answers within a minute.

depends_on.why: it turns the proxy's readers into leaf modules with one short-memory helper and a graph test that forbids the proxy the heavy modules; the host lookup must be one of those leaves and use that helper
its scripts/route-budget.mjs prints the routing-rule count from .next/routes-manifest.json on every build, which is how this step's done-when is read; its graph test holds what src/proxy.ts may reach

the owner asked for no deployment per domain change partly because a deploy is a full build at the edge of its memory; if step 1.29 changed how production is deployed (the build in CI, vercel deploy --prebuilt), the 'deploy' service removed here is the one it left in place

commits.title: A leaf reader answers which store a host belongs to, remembered for a minute

changes.how: A leaf module: it may import only 'server-only', `sql` from 'drizzle-orm', `db` from '@/db/client', `z` from 'zod' with `col` and `typedRow` from './typed-rows' (step 2.20's src/server/site-switch-read.ts, one of the proxy's leaves, imports them too), and `remembered`, `forgetRemembered` and `forgetWhere` from './short-memory' (step 2.20 made src/server/short-memory.ts: remembered(key, load, ms) keeps an answer per instance for ms, shares a load in flight, never remembers a rejected load and caps its memory by clearing it; forgetWhere(predicate) drops every key it matches). It must not import auth.ts, stores.ts, pages.ts, catalog.ts, seo.ts, stripe.ts or src/lib/admin-text.ts. Export type OwnHost = { slug: string; storeId: string; primary: boolean; primaryHost: string | null; language: string | null; market: string | null }. Export async function storeOfOwnHost(host: string): Promise<OwnHost | null>: lower-case the host, strip a port and a trailing dot (as holdingFor() in src/server/holding.ts does); then `return remembered('own-host:' + name, load, 60_000)` (a null answer is remembered like any other; a throw is not), where load runs one statement through typedRow() (z.object({ slug: col.text, store_id: col.uuid, is_primary: col.bool, language: col.textOrNull, market: col.textOrNull, primary_host: col.textOrNull })): select s.slug, s.id as store_id, d.is_primary, d.language, lower(d.market) as market, (select p.hostname from commerce.store_domains p where p.store_id = d.store_id and p.is_primary and p.status = 'active' limit 1) as primary_host from commerce.store_domains d join commerce.stores s on s.id = d.store_id where d.hostname = <host> and d.status = 'active' limit 1 (it uses the unique index store_domains_active_hostname_idx). The shared helper caps the memory itself. A statement that throws is not remembered and is rethrown: the caller decides to leave the request alone. Export function forgetOwnHost(host: string): void { forgetRemembered('own-host:' + <the same normalised name>); } and forgetOwnHosts(): void { forgetWhere((key) => key.startsWith('own-host:')); }. Doc comment: reads the host name only, nothing of the visitor (P6); another instance follows within 60 seconds; a removed domain can answer for up to a minute.

An integration test in the style of src/server/domains.int.test.ts (copy how it makes a store and inserts rows into commerce.store_domains). Cases: an active primary domain gives { slug, primary: true, primaryHost: itself, language: null, market: null }; an active language domain of the same store gives primary false, language 'en' and primaryHost the primary; a market domain gives market in lower case; a domain with status other than 'active' gives null; an unknown host gives null; 'Butikk.Kari.Example:443' finds 'butikk.kari.example'; a second call within the minute sends no statement (count statements with the counter of step 1.9 if it exists, else wrap db() as src/server/assistant-notices-count.int.test.ts does); after forgetOwnHost(host) the next call reads again; a host whose domain row was deleted still answers from memory until forgotten.

It lists the modules src/proxy.ts may import (read it). Add '@/server/host-store' to the allowed list now, so the next commit only changes behaviour. If step 2.20 moved that list into src/server/route-load.graph.test.ts, add src/server/host-store.ts to the proxy's allowed leaves there instead.

changes.how: Today the host's store is storeOfHost(host, storeDomain(), storeHosts()): the compiled list. Add the lookup for a host the compiled list does not know. After ownHostStore is computed: when it is null, the host is not Kaizena Flow's own (hostnameOf(host) !== site, and not the themes or docs host: use the same test mayBeHeld() applies) and not a name under the store domain, call storeOfOwnHost(host) inside a try (a throw logs '[own-host] proxy' and leaves the request alone, exactly as the other jobs do). When it answers a store, do in code what the per-store rules do, in this order, for GET and HEAD: (a) the host is not one the store serves pages on (it is neither the primary nor a language's or a country's own domain) and the store has a primary: 307 to the same path and query on the primary's origin (hostOrigin() of src/lib/paths.ts); (b) otherwise the request is the store's: set the proxy's existing 'house' mechanism for it (the variable that makes out(pathname) return houseServedPath(slug, pathname), so jobs 1, 3 and 5 decide on the request as on a store's own host and what they serve is under /s/{slug}); name the variable for what it now is (served-under-/s by the proxy) and keep job 6's behaviour identical. A lookup that answers null goes on to the holding check as today. Add a job 7 paragraph to the doc comment. The store's files with an extension (robots.txt, store-sitemap.xml, llms.txt, og.png, favicon.ico: ls src/app/s/[store] and src/app/s/[store]/[market] for every route whose name has a dot) are outside the second matcher entry today; add a third entry to config.matcher whose source is a literal alternation of exactly those file names at the root, for example "/(robots\\.txt|store-sitemap\\.xml|llms\\.txt|og\\.png|favicon\\.ico)". A matcher must be a constant (Next's proxy guide, 'matcher values need to be constants'), so it cannot name hosts: the proxy returns NextResponse.next() at once for such a file on Kaizena Flow's own hosts and on {slug}.{store domain} (the compiled generic rule serves those).

It holds the proxy's matcher literals against the constants (read its matcher case). Add: the third matcher entry's file names equal the list of dotted route names found on disk under src/app/s/[store] (computed in the test with fs), so a new store file cannot be forgotten.

Then delete the row, wait 61 seconds (test.slow(); do not add a test-only way to forget the host) and expect the host to stop answering as the store. This holds because playwright.config.ts starts one app server process for the hosts job (one `pnpm start`), so there is one memory; write that in a comment above the wait, and if the config starts more than one app process for this job, stop (see stop_if). Every existing test of the file stays unchanged and green: the compiled rules still serve the seeded domains.
